paragraphs: One-sentence judgment: biological technicians are not operators who just press buttons, but a technical support position that assists biological and medical scientists and makes experiments stable and accurate: set up and operate and maintain laboratory instruments and equipment, monitor experiments, collect data and samples, observe and compute and record results, conduct or assist in research (including collecting samples of blood and water and soil and plants), record production and test data for researchers to evaluate, examine animals and specimens to detect disease or other problems, enter data into databases, isolate and identify and prepare specimens to be tested, monitor whether laboratory work complies with established standards, keep detailed work logs, use computers and computer interface equipment or robotics or high-technology industrial applications, weigh and prepare compounds and solutions for testing or animal feed, clean and maintain and prepare supplies and work areas, set up and adjust and calibrate and clean and maintain and troubleshoot laboratory and field equipment, carry out standardized biological or microbiological or biochemical tests and laboratory analyses, order laboratory equipment and supplies, participate in the research and development or production of drugs and formulations, feed livestock or laboratory animals, analyze experimental data and write reports and summaries of conclusions, carry out or supervise operational projects such as fish hatcheries and greenhouses and livestock production, and provide technical support to scientists and engineers in fields such as agricultural and environmental science or resource management; people who only want ready-made conclusions and are unwilling to trace samples and instruments and records, unwilling to work according to biosecurity and chemical and protective equipment rules, and unwilling to stop, review and report first when data are anomalous or equipment fails or something is beyond their authorization are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to trace a data point back to the sample source and instrument state and record version; you can travel back and forth among the bench and equipment and records over long periods and keep things reproducible; when results deviate or equipment is anomalous or controls fail you are willing to review first and record truthfully rather than picking the data that are usable; you are willing to stop and report first when biosecurity and hazardous chemicals and pathogenic microorganisms are involved or your authorization is exceeded.

Conditions for pausing your investment first: you have not yet completed, under any supervised condition, one full closed loop of confirming the task and constraints, checking samples and data, setting up and operating instruments, observing and recording, reviewing results, and handing over with a trail, or you can only explain your interest by liking biology or being able to use a pipette; nor should you treat having done a laboratory course or being able to use one instrument as proof that you can independently decide the experimental plan or independently handle pathogenic microorganisms and hazardous chemicals and laboratory animal welfare. Biosecurity and chemicals and animal welfare and human-related samples must be handled in accordance with the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and institutional systems and records must be retained; this page does not provide any practice for circumventing regulation.

One sentence: this is a technical position centered on samples and instruments and data records that assists research and testing under biosecurity and quality and reproducibility requirements; the core is setting up and operating and maintaining instruments, monitoring experiments and collecting data and samples, computing and recording results and handing over truthfully, not the imagination of biology; its U.S. wage and employment and industry data are all given in the 19-4021.00 scope for this occupation with labels at every occurrence; on the mainland China side no nationally comparable wage scope corresponding one-to-one to this occupation was obtained, and this page publishes no mainland China wage figures and visibly marks the gap as insufficient evidence.

The work of biological technicians can be divided into three categories: laboratory operations and monitoring (set up and adjust and calibrate and clean and maintain and troubleshoot laboratory and field equipment; carry out biological or microbiological or biochemical tests and laboratory analyses according to standards; weigh and prepare compounds and solutions for testing or animal feed; isolate and identify and prepare specimens to be tested; monitor and observe experiments and record production and test data; clean and maintain and prepare supplies and work areas; feed livestock or laboratory animals when necessary); data and records and compliance (enter data into databases; keep detailed work logs; analyze experimental data and write reports and summaries of conclusions; monitor whether laboratory work complies with established standards; examine animals and specimens to detect disease or other problems; use computers and computer interface equipment or robotics or high-technology industrial applications); and research support and collaboration (conduct or assist in research and collect samples of blood and water and soil and plants; participate in the research and development or production of drugs and formulations; order laboratory equipment and supplies; carry out or supervise operational projects such as fish hatcheries and greenhouses and livestock production; and provide technical support to scientists and engineers in fields such as agricultural and environmental science or resource management). What the three categories share is writing sample sources and instrument states and record versions clearly, rather than taking the desired results first and adding the conditions afterwards.

O*NET2026 this occupation has 18 tasks, 13 core and 5 supplemental, all with importance scores; there are 41 work activities, 21 detailed activities and 57 context items. The core includes research sampling 88, observation and recording 86, animal and specimen examination 84, and data entry 82; drug research and production and feeding animals 85 are supplemental tasks, and it cannot be required that everyone carry out all of them.

Prepare and operate and monitor | Make the experiment runnable | Set up and calibrate and operate instruments and prepare samples according to standard operating procedures, monitor the experimental process and collect data and samples truthfully.

Record and review | Make the results testable | Keep detailed work logs and enter data into databases, review controls and replication and deviations first, and mark the parts needing re-measurement or review.

Maintenance and fault handling | Make the equipment dependable | Clean and maintain and troubleshoot laboratory and field equipment according to procedure, and truthfully record instrument states and calibration and repair situations.

Computing and reporting and handover | Make the results transferable | Compute and organize results and write reports and summaries of conclusions, hand over samples and data and records according to procedure, and do not exaggerate or selectively report results.

Compliance and escalation | Stop risks early | When pathogenic microorganisms or hazardous chemicals or laboratory animals or human-related samples are involved or something is beyond your authorization, report and hand over according to the authorization chain and do not handle it on your own.

entries.answer: Assist biological and medical scientists: set up and operate and maintain laboratory instruments and equipment; monitor experiments; collect data and samples; make observations; and calculate and record results; may analyze organic substances such as blood and food and drugs. Common work includes conducting or assisting experiments and collecting samples such as blood and water and soil and plants; recording production and test data for researchers to evaluate; examining animals and specimens to detect disease or other problems; entering data into databases; isolating and identifying and preparing specimens to be tested; monitoring whether laboratory work complies with established standards; keeping detailed work logs; using computers and computer interface equipment or robotics or high-technology industrial applications; weighing and preparing compounds and solutions for testing or animal feed; cleaning and maintaining and preparing supplies and work areas; setting up and adjusting and calibrating and cleaning and maintaining and troubleshooting laboratory and field equipment; carrying out standardized biological or microbiological or biochemical tests and laboratory analyses; ordering laboratory equipment and supplies; participating in the research and development or production of drugs and formulations; feeding livestock or laboratory animals; analyzing experimental data and writing reports and summaries of conclusions; carrying out or supervising operational projects such as fish hatcheries and greenhouses and livestock production; and providing technical support to scientists and engineers in fields such as agricultural and environmental science or resource management.

entries.answer: Key risks include crossing biosecurity and pathogenic microorganism operation boundaries, compliance risks for human-related samples and biological data, non-reproducible samples and data and records, automated collection and system output being treated as conclusions, hazardous chemicals and laboratory animals and occupational exposure load, and the external reporting and transfer of samples and results beyond authorization; the control approach is to work first within the authorized biosecurity and laboratory quality and ethics scope and carry out risk identification, handle pathogenic microorganisms and chemicals and animals and human-related samples according to procedure and retain records, truthfully record samples and instruments and reagents and lots and data and anomalies, hand over results and provide samples within the authorized scope, and stop and escalate when beyond authorization or when anomalies are found.

hero.quick_answer: Biological technicians assist biological and medical scientists: set up and operate and maintain laboratory instruments and equipment, monitor experiments, collect data and samples, make observations and calculate and record results, and may analyze organic substances such as blood and food and drugs; common work includes conducting or assisting experiments and collecting samples such as blood and water and soil and plants, recording production and test data for researchers to evaluate, examining animals and specimens to detect disease or other problems, entering data into databases, isolating and identifying and preparing specimens to be tested, monitoring whether laboratory work complies with established standards, keeping detailed work logs, using computers and computer interface equipment or robotics or high-technology industrial applications, weighing and preparing compounds and solutions for testing or animal feed, cleaning and maintaining and preparing supplies and work areas, setting up and adjusting and calibrating and cleaning and maintaining and troubleshooting laboratory and field equipment, carrying out standardized biological or microbiological or biochemical tests and laboratory analyses, ordering laboratory equipment and supplies, participating in the research and development or production of drugs and formulations, feeding livestock or laboratory animals, analyzing experimental data and writing reports and summaries of conclusions, carrying out or supervising operational projects such as fish hatcheries and greenhouses and livestock production, and providing technical support to scientists and engineers in fields such as agricultural and environmental science or resource management; their work does not equal the final determination of research conclusions or approval for pathogenic microorganism and animal disposal, nor does it replace the regulatory requirements of the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and institutional systems for biosecurity and laboratory safety and chemicals and laboratory animals and human-derived sample management, and it stops and escalates when sample sources are non-compliant, when situations requiring specific approval such as high-level pathogenic microorganisms or laboratory animals or data export are involved, or when sample contamination or equipment failure or anomalous data or situations beyond one's authorization are found.

subject.summary: Biological technicians assist biological and medical scientists: set up and operate and maintain laboratory instruments and equipment, monitor experiments, collect data and samples, make observations and compute and record results, and may analyze organic substances such as blood and food and drugs; common work includes carrying out biological or microbiological or biochemical tests and laboratory analyses according to standard operating procedures, isolating and identifying and preparing specimens to be tested, setting up and calibrating and maintaining and troubleshooting equipment, keeping detailed work logs, entering data into databases and analyzing data and writing reports and summaries of conclusions, and providing technical support to scientists and engineers in fields such as agricultural and environmental science or resource management.
